risk.title: What does a percentage cost?
risk.intro: The same SL percentage means two very different things depending on what it measures. Both readings are shown below for the same inputs, so the choice can be made against numbers. This answers Q5a in questions.md.
risk.headline: Read as a percentage of price, this stop costs {multiple}× what it costs read as a percentage of margin. The multiple is the leverage.

basisHint.price: The number is a move in the underlying price. A 2% stop means price moves 2%.
basisHint.margin: The number is a fraction of the money committed. A 2% stop means losing 2% of margin, which at 10x is a 0.2% price move.

risk.unreachable: This stop sits at or beyond liquidation. It can never trigger — the position liquidates first.
risk.footnote: Liquidation is simplified: it ignores maintenance margin, fees and funding, so the real liquidation price is slightly closer to entry than shown.

diagHint.socket: WebSocket to the execution engine. Order routing still works over REST while it is down.
diagHint.latency: Measured round trip from this browser to the engine. On a local network it is a millisecond, which says nothing about reaching an exchange.

settings.legalNote: This platform routes real trades for other people's capital. Depending on your jurisdiction and how any fee or profit share is structured, that can require registration or a licence (spec §11). Confirm with a qualified professional before connecting real partner accounts.

login.title: Sign in
login.lede: The panel routes real orders, so it is staff-only.
login.note: No account yet? Create one on the server:

landing.lede: Entry, stop, target, close — each one goes out to every connected account at the same moment, sized to that account's own balance. When one exchange fails, the rest still fill and you get told which one didn't.

diagram.real: Your last trade, leg by leg
diagram.demo: Illustration — connect an account to see your own

isolation.body: Every account gets its own connection, its own rate limit and its own deadline. An exchange going down costs that account the trade and nobody else.

sizing.body: Every account commits 99% of its own USDT. A $50 account and a $5,000 account take the same leverage and the same stop percentage, at very different dollar sizes.

stops.body: Drag the stop on the chart, edit it in the ticket, or change it on the position row — all three push the same amendment to every account.

connect.body: Each account is verified on connect and refused outright if the key can withdraw. Keys are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser.

trade.body: One ticket sets side, leverage and the stop and target percentages. The engine sizes each account from its own balance and dispatches every leg concurrently.

watch.body: Per-leg results arrive as they happen. A failed leg raises a notice that stays on screen until you dismiss it — no toast that disappears while you look away.

coverage.title: Eight exchanges behind one interface
coverage.body: Every exchange implements the same adapter, so capability differences — native versus emulated stops, per-symbol versus per-account leverage — are handled behind the seam rather than in trading logic. Adapters are written from vendored documentation and unit-tested; none has yet been run against a live exchange, so verify on testnet before committing real capital.

security.title: It holds live trading credentials
security.body: Keys are encrypted at rest with rotatable Fernet keys, never logged, never included in an API response, and verified as non-withdrawable at connect time wherever the exchange exposes a permission endpoint. Where it cannot be proven, the account is flagged rather than silently trusted.

landing.footerNote: Order routing and execution. Not an exchange, not a signal service.

connection.exchangeUnmeasured: No exchange round trip measured in the last minute.
